incidents.body:
We are communicating to provide further information on the issues that affected the Actionstep Gmail Add-on platform which started the 1st of June, 2026 and confirm that the issue is now resolved.

What happened:
The Gmail Add-on was running on the deprecated Google Apps Script Rhino runtime. Google ended support for the Rhino runtime, which caused the add-on to fail before any app logic could execute.

What we did:
Our team migrated the Apps Script project to the V8 runtime, created a new deployment version, and redeployed the Gmail Add-on. The add-on is now fully operational.

What we're doing to prevent this:
We have reviewed our runtime dependencies to ensure we are not relying on deprecated infrastructure going forward.

We apologise for any disruption this caused and thank you for your patience.

Regards,
Actionstep Support Team

incidents.body:
**Post-Incident Summary:** United Kingdom – External Connectivity Issue – December 4, 2025

**Incident Overview**    
On December 4, 2025, some customers in the United Kingdom – primarily those using Sky Broadband – experienced difficulty accessing the Actionstep login page. This login page \(also known as the Launchpad\) is hosted in the ap-southeast-2 region; however, no customer data for UK systems is stored or processed in this region. Once a user selects their system, they are directed to the appropriate UK/region-specific server where their data resides.

Our investigation confirmed that this incident was caused entirely by a Sky ISP routing/connectivity issue preventing requests from reaching a wide variety of services hosted in ap-southeast-2. Actionstep also contacted AWS, who confirmed we were one of hundreds of services affected by the Sky outage. There was no issue with the Actionstep platform, AWS infrastructure, or our regional hosting.

The issue began at approximately 2:30 pm GMT on December 4, 2025, and normal access was fully restored by December 9, 2025

**Impact**    
Customers in the UK using Sky Broadband were intermittently or completely unable to reach the Actionstep login page due to Sky’s network routing issue.

Customers using other ISPs, or those switching to an alternative connection such as mobile data, were able to access Actionstep normally.

At all times, the Actionstep platform itself remained operational.

**Resolution**    
Once Sky resolved their connectivity issue, normal access to the Actionstep login page was restored.

Throughout the incident, Actionstep systems continued to perform normally, and users connecting from unaffected networks experienced no disruption.

**Next Steps**    
No Actionstep changes are required, as the root cause was external to our systems and infrastructure.

If customers encounter similar symptoms in the future, we recommend testing an alternative connection \(such as a mobile hotspot\) and contacting their ISP to confirm whether a localised network issue is occurring.

**Acknowledgement**    
We recognise that this caused inconvenience for affected customers and appreciate everyone’s patience while Sky resolved their network routing issue. Ensuring reliable access to Actionstep remains our priority.

**Post-Incident Summary: US – Actionstep Payments Outage – October 17, 2024**

### Incident Overview

On October 17, 2024, Actionstep experienced a service outage affecting the Actionstep Payments platform in the US. A configuration update inadvertently restricted access to a required system resource, which caused payment processing and related services to become temporarily unavailable.

### Impact

US-based customers were unable to process payments or access related payment features for approximately one hour.

### Resolution

The engineering team identified the configuration issue, restored access to the affected resource, and confirmed that all payment services were operating normally. Service was fully restored once functionality was verified across multiple customer accounts.

### Next Steps

We are strengthening our change control and rollout processes to ensure configuration updates are thoroughly tested and deployed safely, with improved monitoring and communication to detect and address issues more quickly.

### Acknowledgement

We sincerely apologize for the disruption this caused to our US customers. Maintaining reliable and uninterrupted access to Actionstep Payments remains a priority.

**Post-Incident Summary:** Microsoft Dependency Disruption – Global – October 29, 2025  

**Incident Overview**    
On October 29, 2025, a widespread outage affecting Microsoft’s Azure Front Door service caused latency, timeouts, and service errors across Microsoft 365 and Azure platforms. This impacted Actionstep features that rely on Microsoft services.  

**Impact**    
During the incident, some users experienced difficulty accessing Microsoft-related functionality, including the Outlook Add-in, OneDrive integrations, and Office 365 email services. Service availability improved as Microsoft began recovery efforts, though intermittent issues persisted for some users.  

**Resolution**    
Microsoft reloaded configurations and rebalanced traffic across its network to restore full operational capacity. As of 23:20 UTC, Microsoft reported significant progress, and Actionstep services dependent on Microsoft systems have largely returned to normal operation.  

**Next Steps**    
Actionstep will continue monitoring Microsoft’s recovery and ensure all integrations remain stable. We are also reviewing dependency monitoring to improve early detection of third-party disruptions.  

**Acknowledgement**    
We appreciate your patience during this incident and apologize for the inconvenience. Ensuring reliable access to all integrated services remains a top priority for Actionstep.

**Post-Incident Summary: North America \(US-East-1\) – AWS Outage Impact – October 20, 2025**

**Incident Overview**    
On October 20, 2025, Actionstep services in the US-East-1 region were affected by a widespread outage within Amazon Web Services \(AWS\). This incident originated from AWS infrastructure and impacted many cloud-based platforms globally, not just Actionstep. As a result, customers experienced degraded performance and intermittent downtime across the Practice Management and Legal Accounting platforms.

**Impact**    
The outage occurred between approximately **9:39 a.m. and 2:19 p.m. MDT**. During this period, some customers in North America experienced slow performance, timeouts, and temporary unavailability of certain features. The issue was entirely due to an AWS infrastructure failure and was not caused by Actionstep systems or changes.

**Resolution**    
AWS restored functionality in the affected region, after which Actionstep systems automatically recovered. Our engineering team closely monitored the recovery process and validated all environments to confirm full stability and normal operation.  
  
For more information about this outage, please see the AWS website: [Service health - Oct 20, 2025 | AWS Health Dashboard | Global](https://health.aws.amazon.com/health/status)

**Next Steps**    
We are reviewing our communication and monitoring processes to ensure faster updates and improved transparency during third-party service disruptions. We are also exploring additional resilience measures to minimize the impact of future upstream provider outages.

**Acknowledgement**    
We understand the disruption this caused and apologize for the impact on your firm’s operations. While this incident originated outside of Actionstep’s control, we remain committed to maintaining system reliability and ensuring clear, timely communication during any service interruption.

### **Post-Incident Summary: Staging Environment Outage – October 13, 2025**

**Incident Overview**  
On October 13, 2025, Actionstep’s Staging environment experienced a temporary service interruption following a system update that affected how application services processed requests.

**Impact**  
Between 11:29 – 12:20 UTC and again 22:16 – 22:33 UTC, users accessing the Staging environment encountered errors and were unable to complete normal testing or pre-release activities.

**Resolution**  
The engineering team identified the update as the cause and restored service by rolling back to a stable configuration. Functionality was verified and all systems in Staging returned to normal operation.

**Next Steps**  
We are refining our deployment and testing procedures to ensure updates to non-production environments are validated without impacting users. Additional automated checks and pre-deployment reviews will be implemented.

**Acknowledgement**  
We apologize for the disruption this caused. Maintaining reliable and predictable environments for testing and validation remains a key priority.
